consolidated_diary:
Model-power mapping from this game, which should be remembered unless future evidence disproves it: qwen/qwen3.5-27b was France, google/gemma-4-31b-it was Austria, anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 was Russia, and deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro was Turkey. The broad lesson from the whole game is that these models were much more predictable by board-verified behavior than by tone. Exact, one-turn, adjudication-testable agreements worked. Broad “trust me” settlements usually did not. However, I pushed this logic too far into static defense and finished on only 5 centers. Next time, keep the board-proof discipline, but convert reliable quiet borders into growth earlier.

qwen/qwen3.5-27b / France was by far the most reliable long-term partner. France agreed to a Piedmont DMZ in 1901 and honored it for the entire game. Repeated reassurances about staying out of Piedmont matched the board every year. Even under heavy external pressure, France stayed south-quiet and kept information flowing. This model seems alliance-capable, non-twitchy, and willing to maintain a stable border if it sees a clear strategic reason. If you can make a clean, low-friction arrangement with qwen early, do it. They appear responsive to reciprocal restraint and consistent messaging. That said, I underused this alliance. France stayed loyal while I gave almost no meaningful military relief, and once France and Germany were weakened, Russia ballooned. Next time, if qwen is your ally, do not just enjoy the quiet border; actively preserve them as a balance piece before they collapse.

google/gemma-4-31b-it / Austria was the clearest “never prepay” opponent. Austria’s pattern was consistent from 1901 onward: soothing language when weak or uncertain, refusal to commit to concrete balancing details, then coercive demands and repeated attempts to retake what it considered “its” space. In Spring 1901 Austria offered a NAP but dodged concrete order transparency. In 1902 it demanded unconditional evacuation of Trieste and immediately attacked it. In 1905 it renewed pressure with VIE->TRI supported by BUD and GRE->ALB to cut cover. In 1907 it escalated to repeated full local attacks. In 1908-1910 it settled into a highly repetitive pressure pattern: BUD-TRI with SER support, TYR-VEN, and ION/AEG-based pressure on ALB or the Ionian route. Even when it paused locally, it was because it was weak or busy elsewhere, not because its aims changed. Against gemma, require step-by-step reciprocity only after adjudication. Demand concrete orders, not atmospherics. Defend with redundancy because it will often attack the same target by multiple cutting routes. If allied with gemma in a future game, assume the alliance is conditional and temporary unless you see repeated costly proof.

anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 / Russia was tactically truthful in narrow windows but strategically the most dangerous long-term actor. Claude repeatedly offered exact one-turn local non-interference deals and often kept them. For example, several times it promised no pressure chain into AEG/ION/GRE/ALB/ADR/TRI and largely honored that. In late 1910 it literally held BUL, CON, and ARM as promised. But this tactical honesty coexisted with relentless strategic growth and flexible coalition behavior. Russia coordinated with Austria against Turkey, supported expansion into the Balkans, rolled through Germany and France, and kept widening its reach west while reassuring me locally. In Fall 1907 Austria even supported SMY-CON while simultaneously attacking me, confirming fresh Austro-Russian coordination on the board. Another important detail: Claude’s promises were often accurate in spirit but not always literally exact. In one phase it said ARM would hold and instead used ARM to support SEV; that did not hurt me directly, but it means wording matters. Against claude, use exact one-turn arrangements only. They can be useful for temporary deconfliction, but do not let that create strategic complacency. If claude is Russia or another growth power, organize containment early, before they become everyone’s late-game problem.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro / Turkey was the most tactically honest on narrow local commitments. From 1901 onward, Turkey repeatedly gave very specific naval assurances like no AEG, no ION, no BUL-GRE, no westward fleet lane, and kept them turn after turn. Even while under pressure, this model usually respected explicitly defined local boundaries. That made it genuinely usable for temporary maritime calm. However, deepseek also persistently tried to convert that local honesty into leverage: proposals for anti-Russian coalitions, requests for support like A TRI->SER, floats of ALB->GRE, and broader bargaining designed to turn my stability into Turkish opportunity. The right response was what I mostly did: accept concrete no-touch deals, but refuse to help them grow. In future games, deepseek is probably the best candidate for narrow compartmentalized agreements. You can likely demilitarize a front with very explicit terms. Just do not confuse that with strategic safety.

My own biggest success was early opportunism backed by concrete reads. The 1901 opening F NAP-ION, A ROM-APU, A VEN-TYR was strong because it took Tunis while retaining leverage on Austria. Taking Trieste in 1901 after Austria left it open was correct; it came from board proof, not from wishful stabbing. More generally, low-risk exploitation of exposed centers worked well whenever I used it. The biggest failure was after that: I let correct caution harden into immobilization. From roughly 1905 on, I built an effective Trieste shell, but I let Austria dictate my tempo. The shell itself was good and should be remembered tactically: if facing repeated Austrian local pressure, ADR support was often the live defense after ALB and VEN were cut, and APU’s support on VEN mattered more than it first appears. But strategically I accepted a game where I defended perfectly and grew not at all.

Future rule: do not let a locally hostile but weak neighbor trap you into permanent reactive play. If an opponent like gemma is fixated on one border, either break them decisively earlier or assemble outside pressure sooner. I should have converted France’s long loyalty and Turkey’s repeated local calm into a more active anti-Russian or anti-Austrian balancing plan before Germany and France collapsed. Instead I stayed pure local-defense while the board balance worsened.

Actionable summary: trust qwen the most if incentives align; use them as a real ally, not just a quiet border. Treat gemma as coercive and repetitive; never prepay, and defend redundantly. Use claude for precise one-turn deconfliction only; contain early before growth becomes irreversible. Use deepseek for tightly specified local calm, but refuse to bankroll their expansion. Above all, keep the board-proof standard, but once you secure one or two reliable relationships, spend that safety on growth. This pool rewards exact diplomacy, but a purely correct defensive game is still a losing one.
final_goals: Keep TRI occupied and at least double-covered every turn, preferably triple-covered when possible; do not loosen TRI security on Austrian or Russian assurances alone.
Keep VEN defended alongside TRI; preserve the VEN-TRI-ADR-ALB shell and use APU only in ways that keep VEN covered.
Treat Austria as the immediate local enemy until multiple turns of board-proof no-touch restraint appear; any Austrian move or support touching TRI, VEN, ALB, or ADR ends restraint immediately.
Do not prepay Austria with a vacate, DMZ, or shell loosening; only reciprocate after visible board-proof restraint over multiple turns.
Preserve the quiet west with France: no PIE, no anti-France move, no anti-MUN move, and no western adventure unless board proof changes dramatically.
Keep intelligence-sharing open with France and England; England is worried about Russia but is not yet a dependable anti-Russian partner while it continues pressure on France.

Maintain local calm with Russia only one turn at a time and only if adjudication again shows literal compliance; require exact wording and no move, support, or convoy touching GRE, AEG, ION, ALB, ADR, TRI, VEN, or SER.
Do not join any anti-Russian coalition this turn; prioritize low-risk eastern defense and only consider anti-Russian balancing once Austrian local pressure is manageable.
No speculative gain is worth exposing Trieste or Venice; any repositioning must preserve the shell first.

After adjudication, reassess first whether Austria attacked locally again, whether Russia literally honored BUL H, CON H, ARM H and kept the corridor quiet, and whether England-Russia strains over French collapse are becoming exploitable.
